acv.quote: It would have been about seventy-five K a year.

header.reason: After a missed Q3, the CFO froze all new vendor projects before the contract was signed, so nobody switched from the homegrown system. Renee calls it timing and says nothing could have been done, but Owen had asked for a payback number in Pikeview's own figures a month earlier, it was never built, and finance saw the project as a 'nice to have.'

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: No single event started this. Owen had wanted to replace a homegrown billing system for a long time, and his only deadline was a new pricing tier that had no date. Without a dated event the deal had no urgency, which suggests our messaging should help champions tie the cost of the old system to a real business deadline.
findings.quote: every pricing change takes them a quarter

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Diane, the CFO, made the final call by freezing all new vendor projects. Renee knows this only through Owen, the champion, and never spoke to her or had her in a meeting. Our whole cycle ran through product and engineering, so the person holding the budget never heard our case.
findings.quote: Owen told me. I never spoke to her.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: No other vendor came up. The real rival was doing nothing, though Renee can only say Owen looked at no one else 'as far as I know.' Near the end Owen's questions shifted from product to finance, and he asked for payback evidence about a month before the freeze.
findings.quote: do you have something that shows payback?

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: The billing demo landed: changing a price in a few clicks, trials and proration got Owen and his engineers excited. The claim that we grow revenue got pushback, which suggests that for this kind of buyer, speed of pricing changes is a stronger lead than revenue growth.
findings.quote: that's a quarter of roadmap in five minutes.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Owen needed a payback number built from Pikeview's own costs: engineering time, billing errors, and subscriptions lost to failed cards. We sent the general ROI deck instead and never added up their numbers. He also asked to speak with a customer who had moved subscriptions without collecting cards again, and only a doc was offered. A tool or session that builds a customer-specific cost case, plus migration references, would have filled the gap.
findings.quote: I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Owen described billing as 'a tax on the roadmap,' a cost holding back his team, while we talked about growing revenue. Finance's words, relayed by Owen, were 'nice to have' and 'if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded.' Our language should describe the cost the old system already imposes, in terms a CFO would fund.
findings.quote: we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap.
